case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread covers a Bluetooth qualification project for a keyboard, including quotation, test planning, execution, and a post-qualification change inquiry. After completing Bluetooth SIG qualification, the customer asks whether adding an additional key code (e.g., Mute) requires requalification. The consultant provides internal guidance and a formal response stating that such a change does not require requalification. The discussion also clarifies when additional product registration may still be needed. Overall, the thread transitions from project execution to post-certification change management.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The core technical question is whether adding a new key code to an already qualified Bluetooth HID keyboard constitutes a design change requiring requalification. The consultant determines that the qualification scope does not explicitly constrain the set of supported key codes, meaning the change does not alter the Bluetooth-compliant design. Since the Report Descriptor structure already includes the relevant capability, adding a key is treated as an extension within the same declared functionality. The distinction is made between changes to Bluetooth functionality (which affect ICS and require requalification) versus application-level usage within an already declared capability. The process implication is that only changes impacting the qualified design or ICS require requalification.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The decision hinges on whether the modification alters the Bluetooth Design as defined in the qualification (i.e., ICS-declared features and compliance-relevant behavior). Since the key addition does not modify the underlying Bluetooth features or ICS declarations, it is considered outside the qualification scope. Therefore, the original qualification remains valid. However, if the product identity changes (e.g., new model name), administrative registration of an additional product under the same Design is required.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If this type of minor change is incorrectly treated as requiring full requalification, it can lead to unnecessary cost, testing effort, and schedule delay. Conversely, if a change that actually impacts the ICS or Bluetooth functionality is mistakenly treated as minor, the product may become non-compliant with Bluetooth SIG requirements. This could lead to enforcement actions or invalid qualification listings, especially if the declared design no longer matches the implemented behavior.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always distinguish between changes to the Bluetooth-qualified design (ICS/features) and changes within already declared functionality. Only modifications that affect the Bluetooth specification implementation require requalification. Functional extensions within an existing declared capability typically do not, but product-level changes (e.g., model variations) may still require administrative listing updates.
